# HLT-C15 eligibility proposal (A2, candidate)

Study: Gulliford M, Naithani S, Morgan M (2006). Continuity of care in type 2 diabetes: patients’, professionals’ and carers’ experiences and health outcomes. Report for the National Co-ordinating Centre for NHS Service Delivery and Organisation R&D (NCCSDO). Revised April 2006, ©NCCSDO 2006 (title page, p.1; footer of every page). Title and year in the brief match the title page.

Proposal: eligible.

## Criterion 1: relationship in a public or publicly funded service
- The object is continuity of care in NHS diabetes care: the relationship between patients with type 2 diabetes and their usual doctor or nurse ("continuous caring relationship"), and coordination between professionals and between general practice and hospital clinics ("seamless service") (p.7, p.140).
- Setting: 19 general practices in two inner-London primary care trusts and hospital diabetes clinics; the project was approved on behalf of Lambeth and Southwark Primary Care Trusts (p.6, p.7, p.41, p.87).
- The study was commissioned by the NHS SDO R&D programme (NCCSDO) (p.1).

## Criterion 2: at least one qualitative and one quantitative finding
- Qualitative: semi-structured interviews with 25 patients (Section 6, p.43-55), 7 carers and 12 South Asian patients (Section 9, p.102-113), 25 professionals (Section 10.3-10.5, p.115-123); thematic / framework analysis.
- Quantitative: ECC-DM patient survey, n=193 analysed (Section 7, p.66-83); cohort study with 10-month follow-up, HbA1c, blood pressure, weight, SF-12 (Section 8, p.86-101); postal survey of 177 professionals (Section 10.6-10.7, p.124-137).

Both criteria are met. Joint claims were not used as a criterion.
